Events


I4C Conducts Exposure Visit and Capacity Building Session for BSF

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, conducted an Exposure Visit and Capacity Building Session for Border Security Force (BSF) personnel to strengthen institutional preparedness against cybercrime. The programme provided participants with insights into India's cybercrime response ecosystem, key initiatives undertaken by I4C, and the evolving cyber threat landscape. It also highlighted collaborative approaches to cybercrime prevention, investigation, and capacity building across agencies. The initiative aimed to enhance knowledge, promote inter-agency coordination, and reinforce collective efforts towards building a cyber-resilient ecosystem through continuous learning, collaboration, and institutional capacity building.

21 July 2026



I4C and University of Delhi Sign MoU for Cyber Safety and Capacity Building

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, and University of Delhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in cybercrime prevention, cyber awareness, and capacity building. The partnership aims to promote cyber hygiene through awareness programmes, workshops, seminars, hackathons, internships, cyber volunteer engagement, and academic initiatives. It will also facilitate research, knowledge sharing, and promotion of cybersecurity education, fostering stronger collaboration between academia and government to build a secure, resilient, and digitally responsible society.

10 July 2026



I4C Conducts Cyber Crime Awareness Session with National Commission for Women

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, in collaboration with the National Commission for Women (NCW), conducted a Cyber Crime Awareness and Capacity Building Session to promote cyber safety and strengthen digital resilience. The session focused on emerging cyber threats targeting women, safe digital practices, cyber fraud reporting mechanisms, and the importance of timely intervention in cybercrime cases. The initiative aimed to equip participants with practical knowledge and reinforce cyber awareness through continued collaboration and capacity-building efforts.

07 July 2026



I4C and RBIH Sign MoU to Strengthen Fight Against Cyber Financial Frauds

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in tackling cyber-enabled financial frauds and curbing mule accounts. The partnership will focus on fraud-risk intelligence sharing, analytical support, and operational coordination to enhance fraud detection and prevention. Under the initiative, I4C's Suspect Registry datasets will support AI-driven fraud detection systems, including MuleHunter.ai™, enabling early identification of suspicious financial activities and reinforcing a secure digital financial ecosystem.

12 May 2026



Workshop on Online Crimes Against Women and Children

I4C imparted training to 175 officers of Uttar Pradesh police on online crimes against women and children in the month of June 2026. The workshop was attended by gazetted officers and cyber unit incharge’s to combat ocwc and effectively handle such cases

22 June 2026



Sundays on Cycle – Cyber Awareness Ride with Fit India

In collaboration with Fit India, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) organised the “Sundays on Cycle – Cyber Awareness Ride” on 15th March 2026 to promote cyber safety through fitness. Over 500 participants took the Cyber Safety Pledge, with many joining awareness quizzes and over 3000 new users subscribed the CYBERDOST social media platforms. The cycling event was graced by hon'ble minister of Delhi Government Sh Ashish Sood. The event highlighted the importance of cyber hygiene and reinforced the message of "Stop. Think. Take Action."

15 March 2026



Union Home Secretary Inaugurates National Dialogue on Online Crimes Against Women and Children

The Union Home Secretary today inaugurated the National Dialogue on Online Crimes Against Women and Children (OCWC) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 9th March 2026. The event was organised by I4C-MHA, with the objective of bringing together key stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening coordinated mechanisms to prevent and effectively respond to online crimes targeting women and children.

09 March 2026



Visit of Hon’ble IT Minister of Mauritius

Delighted to welcome Avinash Ramtohul, Hon’ble IT Minister of Mauritius, to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre on 21st February 2026. With 27 years of distinguished IT experience across the Middle East & Africa, his leadership and insights were truly invaluable.

21 February 2026



Azadi Cyber Crime Se

On the occasion of India’s 79th Independence Day, Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, in collaboration with Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, and Ghaziabad Police, organised “Azadi Cyber Crime Se” – the biggest youth-led awareness movement across Delhi-NCR.

This initiative witnessed 79 powerful street plays on a single day 31st August 2025, performed by Schools, Colleges & Theatre Societies in Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, and Ghaziabad, uniting voices against cybercrime awareness. The event was a grand success as it spread awareness among a large number of students, teachers, parents and citizens in general, through the street plays at 79 different locations.

31st August 2025



One Day Conference on "Cybercrime Awareness and Public Outreach" with Stakeholders

A One-Day Conference on Cybercrime Awareness and Public Outreach was held on 27th June 2025, at the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Delhi.

27th June 2025



Govt. Achievements & Scheme Expo 2025, at ITPO, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), participated in 3 days (21 to 23rd June) Govt. Achievements & Scheme Expo 2025 at Pragati Maidan, New Delhi. wherein several ministers such as Sh. Bhagirath Chaudhary, Sh. K P Malik, Dr. S V Narayan Murthy etc. joined the expo. During the event, various cybercrime awareness sessions were held in which participants/guests/audience engaged. Prominent cybercrime scams and preventive measures were explained and these were captured and subsequently shared through a "Glimpses of Govt. Achievements & Scheme Expo 2025".
